# c0400: Raft browser

## Problem
The tracker is only browsable as directories and `tracker.sh list` output. The user wants to **see and navigate rafts and issues in a browser**: what's active, what's prepped (design ready), what's waiting, and how rafts depend on each other.

Requested (user, 2026-09-29):
- A tool that runs and **produces a self-hosted single-file web app** (one HTML file).
- A list of the **top-level rafts**: those without dependencies. The user clarified that this means no *unfinished* dependencies. **Cursor keys** move up and down the list.
- A **detail pane** for the selected raft: its document, its **reverse dependencies** (the second-level rafts that depend on it), and all its issues.
- **Stable ordering**, so regenerating from the same data produces the same page.
- Rafts and issues rendered nicely with a **JS Markdown renderer**. The user chose a vendored copy inlined into the page, so it works offline.
- **Status shown** for each item: active, prepped (design ready), reviewed, draft, done, and so on.
- **Tabs** at the top to filter: **done**, **active**, **waiting**.
- A **search field**: type any `c`/`d`/`f`/`R` ID to jump to the raft that holds it, with that issue highlighted.
- Decided with the user in prep (2026-09-29):
  - issues that aren't in a raft appear under a **"No raft"** entry at the end of their tab;
  - the command is **`scripts/tracker.sh board [--out PATH] [--open]`**, writing to `.cache/board.html` (gitignored) by default;
  - the renderer is **marked, vendored and inlined**.
- Decided with the user after design-review-001 (2026-09-29):
  - **Active comes from the directory only.** On `main`, rafts go straight from backlog to done (`start` moves them to `active/` on the raft branch), so the Active tab is non-empty only when the page is generated on a raft branch. That's a known limitation.
  - **Only the Waiting tab filters by top level.** Active and Done list every raft in them.
  - **The page's JavaScript is verified by a node smoke test** (AC6).

## Non-goals
- Editing tracker state from the page: it's read-only.
- A live server or file watching: regenerate to refresh.
- Showing review files and spend in detail (a later chore can add them).
- Detecting in-progress rafts from git branches (the user chose directory-only Active).

## Solution
- A new module, `scripts/tracker/board.luau`, reads the tracker tree into a **model**. It computes everything the page needs up front: statuses, raft dependencies both ways, top-level rafts per tab, the "No raft" entries, and a search index. It serializes the model with a small **deterministic JSON writer**.
- An HTML **template**, `scripts/tracker/board.html`, holds the CSS and a small script. The generator inlines the vendored **marked** build and the JSON into it.
- `tracker.sh board` writes the result.
- All the decisions a test can check live in Luau and are specced. The page script only renders the model and handles keys. It's covered by the Observed steps.

## Design

### Files
| path | what |
|---|---|
| `scripts/tracker/board.luau` | the model, the JSON writer, rendering, `build`, the marked pin |
| `scripts/tracker/board.html` | the page template: exactly one `{{MARKED}}` and one `{{DATA}}` placeholder |
| `scripts/tracker/main.luau` | `cmd.board`; the `board` line in `USAGE`; `--open` joins the boolean flags |
| `scripts/vendor/marked.umd.js` | marked **18.0.14** `lib/marked.umd.js`, byte-for-byte |
| `scripts/vendor/marked.LICENSE` | that package's `LICENSE` file, byte-for-byte |
| `.claude/skills/tracker/SKILL.md` | `tracker.sh board [--out PATH] [--open]` under "Other commands" |

**Vendoring**: take both files from the npm tarball `https://registry.npmjs.org/marked/-/marked-18.0.14.tgz` (`package/lib/marked.umd.js` and `package/LICENSE`). The UMD file's sha256 must be `21568877a938d2c4e7d74e27f18e60da96bb73a68809610ca39216e1efebae62` (AC4, checked in prep). It's 46,891 bytes and contains no `</script`. In a browser it defines the global `marked`, with `marked.parse(md)`: GFM, tables included, by default. It's JavaScript, so stylua and selene don't touch it.

### `scripts/tracker/board.luau`
```lua
local store = require("./store")   -- store.isRaftId, store.isIssueId, store.readFront, store.ROOT

export type Tab = "done" | "active" | "waiting"
export type Raft = {
	id: string,            -- "R0040", or "none:<tab>" for a No raft entry
	kind: string,          -- "raft"
	type: string,          -- "feature" | "defect" | "chore" ("" for No raft)
	title: string,         -- frontmatter title ("No raft" for the pseudo entries)
	state: string,         -- "backlog" | "active" | "done", from the directory ("" for No raft)
	design: string,        -- frontmatter design ("" if absent)
	status: string,        -- see Status ("" for No raft)
	single: boolean,       -- frontmatter single == "true"
	pseudo: boolean,       -- true only for No raft entries
	tab: Tab,
	issues: { string },    -- member issue ids, sorted
	dependsOn: { string }, -- raft ids, sorted
	dependents: { string },-- raft ids, sorted
	blockedBy: { string }, -- unfinished dependencies: raft ids and raftless issue ids, sorted
	topLevel: boolean,     -- #blockedBy == 0
	body: string,          -- the document after its frontmatter ("" for No raft)
}
export type Issue = {
	id: string, kind: string, type: string, title: string, state: string, design: string, -- kind is always "issue"
	status: string,
	raft: string?,         -- frontmatter raft; nil when empty or absent
	dependsOn: { string }, -- frontmatter depends_on ids, sorted, as written (even if they don't exist)
	emergent: boolean,     -- frontmatter emergent == "true"
	body: string,
}
export type Model = {
	rafts: { Raft },       -- real rafts sorted by id, then No raft entries in done, active, waiting order
	issues: { Issue },     -- sorted by id
	tabs: { done: { string }, active: { string }, waiting: { string } },
	home: { [string]: string }, -- every raft and issue id -> the id of the entry whose pane shows it (the search index)
	initialTab: Tab,       -- "active" if tabs.active is non-empty, else "waiting"
}

board.MARKED_PATH = "scripts/vendor/marked.umd.js"
board.MARKED_SHA256 = "21568877a938d2c4e7d74e27f18e60da96bb73a68809610ca39216e1efebae62"
board.TEMPLATE_PATH = "scripts/tracker/board.html"

function board.collect(root: string?): Model     -- root defaults to store.ROOT ("tracker")
function board.encode(v: any): string            -- deterministic JSON (below)
function board.render(m: Model, markedJs: string): string
function board.checkMarked(js: string)           -- errors unless sha256(js) == MARKED_SHA256
function board.inlineMarked(js: string): string  -- js minus its trailing "//# sourceMappingURL=…" line
function board.build(root: string?): string      -- read MARKED_PATH, checkMarked, render(collect(root))
```
**`collect(root)`** walks the same layout as `store`: `{root}/{rafts,issues}/[active/|done/]<ID>/<ID>.md` (the layout after c0420; the slug is frontmatter, and the board doesn't read it).
- It takes `state` from the directory, and uses `store.isRaftId`/`isIssueId` for the directory names.
- `store.readFront(path)` supplies the frontmatter. A list value like `[f0100, c0090]` is parsed by taking every `%w+` run, then sorting. The body is everything after the closing `---` line, with leading blank lines dropped.
- Other files in an item's directory (`check.sh`, reviews, `spend.md`, `acceptance/`) are ignored.
- It doesn't use `store.all`, because that is fixed to `store.ROOT`. Specs need a root under `.cache/`.

**Status**: `done` or `active` from the directory; for a backlog item, `ready` or `reviewed` if the design field says so, otherwise `draft`.

**Fields**: `type` is the frontmatter `type` if it's `feature`, `defect` or `chore`, otherwise `""`. `title` and `design` default to `""`, and booleans to false. A document without frontmatter keeps its whole text as `body`. `collect` never errors on missing fields.

**Membership and dependencies**:
- **Membership**: an issue belongs to the raft named by its own `raft:` field, and that raft must exist. That's how `tracker.sh members` works, and it covers emergent issues. The raft's own `issues:` list is ignored. **If the named raft doesn't exist, the issue's `raft` is nil**, so it counts as raftless and lands in a No raft entry, never nowhere.
- **`raft.dependsOn`**: the sorted set of rafts R such that some member issue's `depends_on` names an issue whose raft is R, with R ≠ this raft. Ids that don't exist, and issues without a raft, add nothing.
- **`dependents`** is the reverse, sorted.

**Blocked and top level** (design-review-001 F3):
- `blockedBy` is the sorted set of every raft in `dependsOn` whose status isn't `done`, plus every **raftless** issue named in a member's `depends_on` whose status isn't `done`.
- A raft is top level when `blockedBy` is empty. No dependencies counts as top level.

**Tabs**: raft state `done` → `done`, `active` → `active`, `backlog` → `waiting`.
- `tabs.done` and `tabs.active` list **every** real raft in that tab. `tabs.waiting` lists only the **top-level** real rafts (user, after design-review-001 F4).
- Each list is sorted by id and ends with that tab's No raft entry, `none:<t>`, if it's non-empty.
- A No raft entry holds the issues without a raft whose state maps to `t`, sorted. Its `topLevel` is true, `single` false, `blockedBy` and `dependsOn` empty, and `dependents` as below. An empty No raft entry is omitted everywhere.
- **No raft entries have `dependents` too** (design-review-002 F5): the sorted rafts with a member whose `depends_on` names an issue in that entry. So a raft blocked only by a raftless issue is reachable from the No raft entry's pane, as well as by search.
- A blocked waiting raft is reachable through its blockers' Dependents (raft or No raft) or Waiting-for links, **unless every blocker is itself unreachable in the list**. Two waiting rafts that block only each other are reachable only by search. That's accepted: a cycle is a tracker error that the board makes visible, rather than hides (design-review-003 F3).
- `initialTab` is `active` if `tabs.active` is non-empty, else `waiting`.

**`home`**: every real raft maps to itself. Every member issue maps to its raft, and every raftless issue maps to its `none:<tab>` entry. Pseudo ids aren't keys.

**`encode`** (deterministic; Lune's `serde.encode` writes an empty table as `{}`, which the page can't iterate):
- **Strings**: `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\r` and `\t` are escaped. Other control characters become `\u00XX`, and **`<` becomes `\u003c`**, so no data can end the `<script>` element.
- **Tables**: an empty table becomes `[]`, since every empty table in the model is a list. A table with `#t > 0` becomes an array in order. Anything else becomes an object with its keys **sorted**.
- **Scalars**: booleans become `true`/`false`, and numbers use `tostring`. Any other type is an error.

**`inlineMarked`** removes the final `\n//# sourceMappingURL=…` line, so a browser never tries to fetch `marked.umd.js.map`. `render` inlines `inlineMarked(markedJs)`.

**`render(m, markedJs)`**: find `{{MARKED}}`, then `{{DATA}}`, in the **template text before any substitution**, and assemble the pieces around them. That way text inside marked or the data can never be taken for a placeholder. Never use `string.gsub` with these values: marked's source is full of `%`.

**Stability**: the output depends only on the tracker's files and the vendored marked.
- No timestamps, and no paths.
- Every list is sorted, and object keys are sorted by `encode`.
- AC2 writes the same fixture in two orders and two locations, and requires identical bytes.

### `SETUP.md`
Once `done` promotes `smoke.spec.luau` into `tests/acceptance/c0400/`, `scripts/check.sh --full` needs `node`. Add it to the Prerequisites table:
- macOS: `brew install node`;
- Linux: distro packages;
- CI: preinstalled on GitHub runners.

A missing `node` makes the smoke spec fail with a clear message.

### `tracker.sh board` (`cmd.board` in `main.luau`)
- `out = opts["--out"][1]` or `.cache/board.html`. Relative paths resolve against the repo root, since `tracker.sh` changes to it. Create its directory, write `board.build()`, and print `out`.
- With `--open`, run `open` on macOS and `xdg-open` otherwise. If that fails, print a warning to stderr: the command still succeeds, because the page was written.
- **`--open` must be added to `flags()`'s boolean list** next to `--single`, `--stdout` and `--include-active`. Otherwise it eats the next argument (found in prep).
- Add `board [--out PATH] [--open]` to `USAGE`, inside the `[[ … ]]` string.

### The page (`board.html`; about 150 lines in the prep prototype)
- **Layout**:
  - a header with the title `pickman tracker`;
  - tab buttons `#tab-active`, `#tab-waiting` and `#tab-done`, in that order (workflow order; the current one highlighted);
  - a search `<input id="search">`;
  - below that, the list `<ul id="list">` on the left and the pane `<section id="pane">` on the right.
- **Script placement** (design-review-002 F1): the page script is the **last element of `<body>`**, after the `board-data` script and every element it looks up. At that point those elements exist in a browser, and in AC6's fake DOM, which during load returns only elements that come before the running script. (Wrapping the script in `DOMContentLoaded` would also work, and AC6 fires that event after loading.)
- The head starts with `<meta charset="utf-8">` (tracker documents contain non-ASCII). Styles are inline (light and dark via `prefers-color-scheme`). Nothing loads from the network. `<script>{{MARKED}}</script>` sits in the head, and `<script type="application/json" id="board-data">{{DATA}}</script>` sits before the page script.
- **List**: `tabs[current]`, one row each (an empty tab shows a single "Nothing here" row): the id (`—` for No raft), the title, a status badge and the issue count. The selected row is highlighted and scrolled into view.
- **Keys** (ignored while the search field has focus):
  - ↓/↑ move the selection, clamped;
  - →/← switch tab (cycling);
  - `/` focuses search.
- The first tab shown is `initialTab`. Switching tabs selects the first row.
- When the pane shows an entry that isn't in the list (after a search, no row is selected), ↓ selects the first row and ↑ the last.
- Every title, id and `depends_on` value put into HTML by the script is HTML-escaped. Only `marked.parse` output is inserted raw.
- **Pane** for the selected entry:
  - `id`, title and badge;
  - type, "single issue" and design;
  - **Waiting for** (`blockedBy`), **Depends on** and **Dependents** lists, with exactly those headings, each entry a link with its title and badge;
  - every id link in the pane is `<a class="jump" data-id="<ID>">`, and a click on the pane is handled through `event.target.closest("a.jump")` and its `data-id` (AC6 clicks one);
  - **Issues**, one `<details id="i-<ID>">` each: the summary is a link with the id, title, badge and its `depends_on`, and the body is rendered with `marked.parse`;
  - then the raft's own document, rendered.
  - Clicking any id link shows that item as a search would.
- **Search**: Enter looks the query up in `home`, case-insensitively: `r0040` means `R0040`, and `F0100` means `f0100`.
  - A match switches to that entry's tab, selects it if it's in the list, shows its pane, and opens, highlights and scrolls to the issue. The issue's `<details>` gets class `highlight` and the `open` attribute.
  - A dependent (not top-level) raft shows in the pane with no list row selected.
  - No match adds class `miss` to the field (shown red), and a hit removes it. Esc leaves the field.
  - Successful jumps update `location.hash` (`#c0390`), and loading the page with a hash jumps there.
- Badge colours: done grey, active blue, ready green, reviewed amber, draft light grey.
- **DOM subset** (design-review-001 F1). The page script may use only what AC6's fake DOM provides:
  - `document.getElementById` for the ids above and `board-data`, plus `document.addEventListener`;
  - `document.querySelector`, which may return null in the test, so it's used only for optional scrolling;
  - on elements: `innerHTML`, `textContent` (of `board-data`), `value`, `classList.add/remove/toggle/contains`, `addEventListener`, `focus`, `blur`, `select`, `scrollIntoView` and `scrollTop`;
  - on events: `key`, `target` and `preventDefault`;
  - plus `location.hash`, `history.replaceState` and `marked.parse`.
  - Clicks on list rows and pane links may use `event.target.closest`. The smoke test clicks a pane link through `closest("a.jump")`, but not list rows (OC1 covers those).
  - The keydown handler ignores events whose `target` is the search field.

### Scalability
- **Size**: `collect` reads each document once. The real tracker's page is about 250 KB (prep prototype, 45 items), about 47 KB of it marked, growing linearly with the tracker's text.
- **Speed**: the page renders one pane at a time, calling `marked.parse` only for the items shown. Generation is well under a second.

### Maintainability
- **The model is the contract.** Later additions (review files, spend) are new fields in `collect` and new sections in the pane, and the existing specs stay valid.
- **Upgrading marked**: replace the two vendored files and change `MARKED_SHA256`. That's a chore, since it touches the promoted AC4 spec. The pin makes an accidental change loud.

### Usability
- **Keyboard first**: arrows, `/` then Enter, and `#id` deep links, which are shareable locally.
- **Findable**: every item is reachable, either as a top-level entry, through a Depends-on/Dependents link, or by search.
- **One command**: regenerate with `tracker.sh board --open`.

### Touched modules
- `SETUP.md` (node is now needed for the full gate, design-review-002 F4)
- `scripts/tracker/board.luau`
- `scripts/tracker/board.html`
- `scripts/tracker/main.luau`
- `scripts/vendor`
- `.claude/skills/tracker/SKILL.md`

### Affected specs
`lune run scripts/affected -- scripts/tracker/board.luau scripts/tracker/main.luau` prints `ALL`, because `scripts/` changes force a full run. New specs: the five acceptance specs, plus the executor's own under `tests/tooling/`.

## Unknowns & experiments
- **E1 (run in prep: PASS)**: can marked be vendored and inlined, and does it render in a browser context?
  - marked 18.0.14's `lib/marked.umd.js` (MIT, 46,891 bytes, sha256 above) contains no `</script`.
  - Run in a Node `vm` sandbox with no `module` (like an inline `<script>`), it defines only the global `marked`. `marked.parse` renders headings, lists, inline code and GFM tables.
- **E2 (run in prep: PASS)**: can Lune hash and write deterministic JSON?
  - `serde.hash("sha256", …)` matches `shasum -a 256`.
  - `serde.encode` sorts keys, **but writes empty tables as `{}`**. The prototype page crashed on that (the real tracker's Active tab was empty), which is why the design has its own `encode`, and AC2 pins `[]`.
- **E3 (run in prep: PASS)**: a prototype of this design (board about 290 lines, template about 150, `cmd.board` about 15) passed the four specs of that time (21 cases) with `luau-lsp analyze` at 0 errors; after the review rounds it passes all five (28 cases).
  - `node --check` accepts both inline scripts of the generated page.
  - After design-review-001 there are five specs (27 cases). The model mutants "top-level filter on every tab", "raftless deps don't block", "unknown raft kept" and "source map kept" also fail.
  - Mutation check: the specs fail for each of these twelve wrong implementations:
    - any dependency blocking top level;
    - status ignoring design;
    - dangling `depends_on` counted;
    - empty No raft entries kept;
    - unrafted issues always homed to waiting;
    - empty lists as `{}`;
    - `<` not escaped;
    - frontmatter kept in bodies;
    - keys unsorted;
    - the pin not checked;
    - `--out` ignored;
    - issues unsorted.
  - Found in prep: `--open` needs the boolean-flag list, and the `USAGE` string's `]]` must end after the new line.
- **E4b (after design-review-002)**: the harness models load order and focus, tracks `preventDefault`, and presses every key, including ← and arrows typed into the search field.
  - A second "quiet" page, with no active rafts, covers opening on Waiting and an empty Active tab.
  - The reviewer's scenarios check out: a page with its script in `<head>` fails AC6, as it does in a browser, while the same script on `DOMContentLoaded` passes.
  - These fail AC6: ← doing nothing; `/` without `preventDefault`; keys typed into search not ignored; Esc not leaving search; a search hit not switching the list's tab; `initialTab` ignored.
- **E4 (run in prep: PASS)**: can the page script be driven headless? `smoke.spec.luau` renders a fixture page and runs its inline scripts under node against a small fake DOM (the subset above). It walks tabs, arrows, search with case folding, highlighting, an unknown id, tab clicks and a `#id` on load.
  - It catches eight wrong page scripts: search case-sensitive; no highlight; ↓ broken; tab keys not cycling; the hash ignored; unknown id not marked; markdown not rendered; the initial tab wrong.
  - node is not in `rokit.toml`, but it's preinstalled on GitHub's runners and on this machine. The spec fails with a clear message if it's missing.
- **Residual**: layout, colours and click targets need a browser (OC1).

## Regression guard
- **Tooling specs**: `tests/tooling/spend.spec.luau`, `affected.spec.luau` and the promoted c0010 tracker-lifecycle spec exercise `main.luau`. The `--open` flag change must not alter other flags.
- **The full gate runs anyway**, since `scripts/` changed. The generated page lands in the gitignored `.cache/` (R0060 RC1).

## Test plan
- **`acceptance/model.spec.luau`** → AC1. On a 16-document fixture written under `.cache/` (it includes a raft blocked only by a raftless issue, an issue naming a missing raft, and an active raft blocked by a waiting one):
  - sorted ids;
  - statuses;
  - fields;
  - bodies without frontmatter;
  - dependencies both ways (including a dangling id);
  - `blockedBy` and top level;
  - tabs (only Waiting filtered) with No raft last;
  - `initialTab`;
  - the No raft entries (empty ones omitted);
  - `home`.
- **`acceptance/page.spec.luau`** → AC2:
  - identical bytes across two write orders and locations, with no path leak;
  - a DOCTYPE, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `inlineMarked(marked)` inlined exactly once with no `sourceMappingURL`, and no external `src`/`href`/`<link>`/`@import`;
  - the data decodes to the model;
  - empty lists as `[]`, and `encode`'s exact output;
  - `<` escaped, so an issue body containing `</script><script>` round-trips;
  - the element ids the page is driven by.
- **`acceptance/cli.spec.luau`** → AC3:
  - `--out` is written and printed, and equals `board.build()`;
  - the default `.cache/board.html`;
  - the real tracker's page covers every raft and issue directory.
- **`acceptance/vendor.spec.luau`** → AC4: the pinned path and sha, the licence text, and `checkMarked` refusing a tampered file.
- **`acceptance/smoke.spec.luau`** → AC6: node drives the generated page against the fake DOM (E4, E4b). Three runs:
  - `walk`, on the full fixture: every key, focus, search and tab clicks;
  - `quiet`, a fixture without active rafts: it opens on Waiting, and an empty tab shows "Nothing here";
  - `hash`: `#c0050` on load.
- **The executor's own `tests/tooling/board.spec.luau`**:
  - `encode` of nested, unicode and control characters;
  - `collect` on an empty tree (no tracker dirs), which gives empty lists and tabs.

### Rules and mutants
R0070's table, added to this prep after the design was approved. A row is `run` only where E3, E4 or E4b above record that the mutant was planted on the prep prototype and the case failed; every other row is `reasoned` (not run).

| rule | spec :: case | mutant it kills | checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| Items are listed sorted by id (rafts, then No raft entries, then issues) | `model :: lists rafts, then the No raft entries, and issues, each sorted by id` | issues unsorted | run (E3) |
| Status comes from the directory and the design field | `model :: derives a status …` | status ignoring design | run (E3) |
| Fields and bodies: frontmatter is not part of the body | `model :: keeps each item's fields …`, `keeps the markdown body …` | frontmatter kept in bodies | run (E3) |
| Raft dependencies come from member issues' `depends_on`, both ways; dangling ids add nothing | `model :: derives raft dependencies …` | a dangling `depends_on` counted | run (E3) |
| `blockedBy` covers unfinished rafts and raftless issues; done dependencies don't block | `model :: blockedBy lists …`, `a raft is top level …` | any dependency blocking top level; raftless deps don't block | run (E3) |
| Only Waiting filters by top level; Done and Active list every raft; No raft entry last | `model :: Done and Active list every raft …` | top-level filter on every tab | run (E3) |
| An issue naming a missing raft is raftless | `model :: collects issues without a raft …` | unknown raft kept | run (E3) |
| Raftless issues get a No raft entry per tab; empty entries are omitted | `model :: collects issues without a raft …`, `maps every raft and issue id …` | empty No raft entries kept; unrafted issues always homed to Waiting | run (E3) |
| `initialTab` is Active when it has entries, else Waiting | `model :: opens on Active …`, `smoke :: with nothing active …` | `initialTab` ignored | run (E4b) |
| Deterministic JSON: sorted keys, empty lists as `[]`, `<` escaped, data decodes back to the model | `page :: embeds the model …`, `writes empty lists …`, `escapes < …` | keys unsorted; empty lists as `{}`; `<` not escaped | run (E3) |
| marked is inlined once without its source-map comment | `page :: inlineMarked drops only …` | source map kept | run (E3) |
| The vendored marked is the pinned file and `build` refuses a tampered one | `vendor :: is the pinned file`, `build refuses …` | the pin not checked | run (E3) |
| The page is byte-stable regardless of write order or location, with no path or timestamp | `page` (AC2 cases) | a path or timestamp embedded | reasoned |
| The licence ships beside marked | `vendor :: ships with marked's MIT licence …` | licence file missing | reasoned |
| `board` writes `--out` and prints it; the default is `.cache/board.html` | `cli :: writes --out …`, `defaults to …` | `--out` ignored; a different default | run (E3: `--out`); default reasoned |
| The real tracker's page covers every raft and issue | `cli :: the real tracker's page shows …` | a state directory skipped | reasoned |
| The page script: tabs, arrows (clamped), `/` with `preventDefault`, Esc, search (case-insensitive, highlight, tab switch, unknown id marked), `#id` on load, pane links jump | `smoke :: drives the page …`, `opens the item named by #id on load` | the eight wrong page scripts of E4 and the six of E4b | run (E4, E4b) |

## Acceptance criteria

### Checked
- **AC1**: `board.collect(root)` builds the designed model: items sorted by id, a status from state and design, raft membership from issues' `raft:` (a missing raft means raftless), raft dependencies and dependents from `depends_on` (dangling ids ignored), `blockedBy` covering unfinished rafts and raftless issues, top level meaning nothing blocks the raft, Done and Active tabs listing every raft and Waiting only top-level rafts, a non-empty No raft entry last, `initialTab`, and a `home` for every id.
- **AC2**: `board.render` produces one self-contained UTF-8 HTML document: byte-identical for identical tracker data regardless of write order or location, marked inlined once without its source-map comment, nothing loaded from elsewhere, the model embedded as JSON that decodes back to it (empty lists as `[]`, `<` escaped), and the tab, search, list and pane elements present.
- **AC3**: `scripts/tracker.sh board` writes `board.build()` to `--out` or `.cache/board.html` and prints the path. On the real tracker, it shows every raft.
- **AC4**: `scripts/vendor/marked.umd.js` is marked 18.0.14, pinned by sha256 and verified by `board.checkMarked`, with marked's licence beside it.
- **AC5**: The tracker skill documents `tracker.sh board`, its `.cache/board.html` default and `--open`.
- **AC6**: The generated page's scripts run. Driven under node against the designed DOM subset, with elements existing only once parsed:
  - the page opens on `initialTab` (Waiting when nothing is active), and an empty tab shows "Nothing here";
  - ←/→ cycle tabs, and ↓/↑ move the selection, clamped (↓ from an unlisted pane selects the first row);
  - `/` focuses search with `preventDefault`, keys typed into search are ignored, and Esc leaves it;
  - search finds any id case-insensitively, switches the list to its tab and highlights the issue;
  - an unknown id marks the field;
  - a tab click switches tabs, and `#id` in the URL opens that item;
  - a jump updates `location.hash`;
  - the pane shows Waiting for, Depends on and Dependents, with id links, and clicking one jumps there;
  - ↑ from an unlisted pane selects the last row.

### Judged
None.

### Observed
- **OC1** (any browser): run `scripts/tracker.sh board --open`. Then:
  1. On `main`, Active is empty (the known limitation), so the page opens on Waiting, with badges. ↓/↑ move the selection, and the pane follows. →/← switch tabs.
  2. A raft's pane shows its rendered document, including tables and code, its Depends on and Dependents links, and its issues as expandable rendered sections.
  3. The Waiting tab ends with a "No raft" entry listing the unrafted issues.
  4. Press `/`, type `c0390`, and press Enter: the Done tab opens on R0050 with c0390 expanded and highlighted. Typing `r0040` shows R0040 in the pane and switches the list to its tab. An unknown id turns the field red.
  5. Reloading with `#f0110` in the URL jumps to it. Clicking an id link in the pane jumps there.
  6. Regenerating without tracker changes produces the same file (also RC1).

## Implementation steps
1. Vendor marked from the npm tarball and check the sha. Then `board.MARKED_*` and `checkMarked`. Run AC4. Commit.
2. `collect`, with the frontmatter list parsing and the model rules. Run AC1. Commit.
3. `encode`, `inlineMarked`, the template and `render`, then `build`. Run AC2 and AC6. Commit.
4. `cmd.board`, `USAGE`, and the `--open` flag. Run AC3 and try the page in a browser (OC1). Commit.
5. The tracker skill line, and node in `SETUP.md`. Run AC5, `scripts/check.sh --full` and `scripts/tracker.sh check R0060`. Commit.
